newsitem.title: SPAIN: Spain likely to meet '97 inflation goal of 2.6 pct.
newsitem.headline: Spain likely to meet '97 inflation goal of 2.6 pct.

text.p: Spain is likely to meet its 1997 inflation target of 2.6 percent, the Economy Ministry said on Wednsday.
In a statement, released after the December CPI, the Spanish Ministry said expectations for the current year are positive.

"Because we made the 1996 target, automatic increases won't take effect, the downtrend in the interest rates will reduce costs, tariffs will experience some reductions...All these factors are solid enough to make it likely that Spain will meet its target," the statement said.
December CPI rose 0.3 percent month-on-month for a 3.2 percent year-on-year rate, unchanged from November. That was well below the government's early target of 3.4 percent.
In the statement, the Ministry reemphasised the need for only modest increases in wages.
Spain's Economy Ministry added that the data are a big step toward meeting Maastricht's convergence criteria and laying the base for moderate inflation this year.
Spain's government forecast to end 1997 at 2.6 percent, with December over December figures increasing.
